# 129 · A batch commit made the batch record's method, proved equal on the batch's components

[← All examples](../README.md)

| Verdict | Categories | Severity if shipped | Change | Verified unit | Approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **✓ Verified: equivalent on every input** | functional, no-false-positive | none | refactor, behaviour change not intended | [`Batch#offsetToCommit`](../../examples/apps/crosscut/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/crosscut/kafka/BatchCommit.java) | [B9: Regression verification](../../lib/README.md) |

> The same refactor as example 128, the batch's start and size gathered into a record `Batch(start, size)` with the commit arithmetic as its method and the guard on the batch in its compact constructor, with the check on the failed index kept in the method, since the index is no component. The regression proof relates the record's method to the static function called with the components and proves them equal on every batch the constructor accepts and every index, in half a second.

Tags: [messaging](../README.md#tag-messaging), [dropped-case](../README.md#tag-dropped-case), [record-components](../README.md#tag-record-components), [signature-change](../README.md#tag-signature-change)

## The change

Introduce a parameter object: the batch's start and size become the record `Batch(long start, int size)`, `offsetToCommit(int failedIndex)` its method, and `NONE_FAILED` its constant. The compact constructor refuses a negative start and an empty batch; the method keeps the check that the failed index is `NONE_FAILED` or within the batch, and the arithmetic. The test class is renamed with the kernel, and its four tests pass: the whole batch committed when nothing failed, the commit up to the failed record, an empty batch refused, and an index past the batch refused.

The method's signature changed, so the developer states how the previous version is called from the new parameters: `net.terminalvalue.crosscut.kafka.BatchCommit#offsetToCommit(this.start, this.size, failedIndex)`. The verifier proves that on every input, the new method agrees with the previous one called that way, or shows one on which it does not.

**Before** ([`BatchCommit.java`](../../examples/apps/crosscut/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/crosscut/kafka/BatchCommit.java), line 1):

```java
package net.terminalvalue.crosscut.kafka;

/**
 * Which offset a batch listener commits after a batch, in the semantics of Spring Kafka's {@code DefaultErrorHandler}
 * for a {@code BatchListenerFailedException}: the records before the one that failed are done, the failed record and
 * every record after it are redelivered. A committed offset is the next record to read, so it is one past the last
 * record that is done.
 */
public final class BatchCommit {

    private BatchCommit() {}

    /** No record of the batch failed. */
    public static final int NONE_FAILED = -1;

    /**
     * The offset to commit for a batch of {@code batchSize} records starting at {@code batchStart}, given the index
     * within the batch of the record that failed, or {@link #NONE_FAILED}.
     */
    public static long offsetToCommit(long batchStart, int batchSize, int failedIndex) {
        if (batchStart < 0 || batchSize <= 0 || failedIndex < NONE_FAILED || failedIndex >= batchSize) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("batchStart >= 0, batchSize > 0 and -1 <= failedIndex < batchSize are required");
        }
        return failedIndex == NONE_FAILED ? batchStart + batchSize : batchStart + failedIndex;
    }
}
```

**After:**

```java
package net.terminalvalue.crosscut.kafka;

/**
 * A batch a batch {@code @KafkaListener} received: the offset of its first record and how many records it holds,
 * and which offset to commit after it, in the semantics of Spring Kafka's {@code DefaultErrorHandler} for a
 * {@code BatchListenerFailedException}: the records before the one that failed are done, the failed record and
 * every record after it are redelivered. A committed offset is the next record to read, so it is one past the last
 * record that is done.
 */
public record Batch(long start, int size) {

    /** No record of the batch failed. */
    public static final int NONE_FAILED = -1;

    public Batch {
        if (start < 0 || size <= 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("start >= 0 and size > 0 are required");
        }
    }

    /** The offset to commit, given the index within the batch of the record that failed, or {@link #NONE_FAILED}. */
    public long offsetToCommit(int failedIndex) {
        if (failedIndex < NONE_FAILED || failedIndex >= size) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("-1 <= failedIndex < size is required");
        }
        return failedIndex == NONE_FAILED ? start + size : start + failedIndex;
    }
}
```

## What the verifier found

For every input, the new code returns what the old code returned, or throws what it threw, the old code being called with the arguments `this.start, this.size, failedIndex` computed from the new parameters.

This is a proof over the whole domain (this: Batch(start: long, size: int) × failedIndex: int), not a sample. JBMC turned the statement into a satisfiability problem over the bytecode of both versions and showed that it has no solution: no input exists on which they differ.

## Would the existing tests have caught it?

Every existing unit test passes, as it should (`java -ea net.terminalvalue.crosscut.Tests`, run against the patched code).

## Why it matters

None: the record's method agrees with the static function on every batch the constructor accepts and every index. A start or size the constructor rejects was refused by the function too, with the same exception, so a listener that built a `Batch` from what it received sees what it saw.

## Why the verdict is right

The regression proof relates the record's method to the static function it replaced with `previousArguments` over the record's components and the method's parameter, `this.start, this.size, failedIndex`: the harness takes the three as symbolic inputs, builds the `Batch` in the new version only, calls the function on the components and the method on the record, and JBMC proves the two outcomes equal over every input the constructor accepts, two properties in 0.5 s. The split of the guard, batch in the constructor and index in the method, is what the proof confirms: on an index outside the batch both versions throw `IllegalArgumentException`, on one inside both commit the same offset.

## What to do

Nothing to fix. The example is the control for 128: the same refactor with the guard split as the components dictate, which the proof accepts.

## Notes

- The library's run of this shape took 0.5 s with JBMC: three stages, two properties (the assertion and the unwinding assertion of the harness's loops), proved over `this: Batch(start: long, size: int) × failedIndex: int`. The measurement on this kernel is the pipeline's.
- The relation between the versions is the new one of this cycle: a static method that became a method of a record is related to its previous version by `previousArguments` (the tool's `--before-arguments`) over the record's components, `this.start, this.size, failedIndex`, with `previousSymbol` (`--before-target`) naming the function as it was. The harness takes the components and the index as its symbolic inputs, builds a `Batch` from the components in the new version only (there is no record in the previous one), skips an input the constructor rejects, calls the function on the components and the method on the record, and asserts that the two outcomes agree. The generated statement reads `net.terminalvalue.crosscut.kafka.Batch this_after; // the previous version takes the components` and `a = before.net.terminalvalue.crosscut.kafka.BatchCommit.offsetToCommit(batchStart_, batchSize_, failedIndex_)`. The other direction, a record's method made static, is refused: the previous version's record would have to be built from expressions.
- The patch changes the kernel and its test, with the test class renamed and the test of an index past the batch kept or dropped with the check. The module's property on the static function (example 032, `src/contract/properties.contract`) and its API contract are not in the patch: the property proof (`prove`) takes static methods only, so the property would have to be restated on a static entry point, a limit of the tool noted in `lib/README.md`, and the regression proof is the check this example is about.
- Gap scan (step 1a of `llm-dlc/loops/sound-verdicts.md`, 5 November 2026, JDK 25.0.4.1, from the bytecode, nothing proved): the tool's own checker meets no gap in the 2 methods the proof reaches in either version, so strict mode does not move this verdict. The recorded proof is JBMC's, which strict mode of the tool's own checker does not change. JBMC's own approximations are step 4c's.

## Evidence

How the verdict was reached: JBMC 6.11.0: 2 properties proved over this: Batch(start: long, size: int) × failedIndex: int in 0.3 s; loops unwound 16 times with unwinding assertions.

This result was recorded before runs fingerprinted their inputs, so whether it still matches the current patch and sources is not known.

```java
/** Generated by jvmcontract: asserts that two versions of a method agree. The class file JBMC checks is generated directly; this is the same statement, for readers. */
public final class EquivalenceHarness {
    public static void check(long this_start, int this_size, int failedIndex) {
        // The records, from their components, in both versions; an input a constructor rejects is outside the statement.
        net.terminalvalue.crosscut.kafka.Batch this_after; // the previous version takes the components
        try { this_after = new net.terminalvalue.crosscut.kafka.Batch(this_start, this_size); } catch (Throwable t) { return; }
        // The previous version's arguments, from the new parameters; an input for which one throws (a record its constructor rejects) is outside the relation.
        long batchStart_ = this_start; int batchSize_ = this_size; int failedIndex_ = failedIndex;
        long a = 0;
        int ea = 0;
        try { a = before.net.terminalvalue.crosscut.kafka.BatchCommit.offsetToCommit(batchStart_, batchSize_, failedIndex_); } catch (java.lang.NumberFormatException t) { ea = 1; } catch (java.lang.ArithmeticException t) { ea = 2; } catch (java.lang.NullPointerException t) { ea = 3; } catch (java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException t) { ea = 4; } catch (java.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException t) { ea = 5; } catch (java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException t) { ea = 6; } catch (java.lang.NegativeArraySizeException t) { ea = 7; } catch (java.lang.ClassCastException t) { ea = 8; } catch (java.lang.IllegalStateException t) { ea = 9; } catch (java.lang.IllegalArgumentException t) { ea = 10; } catch (java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException t) { ea = 11; } catch (java.util.NoSuchElementException t) { ea = 12; } catch (java.util.ConcurrentModificationException t) { ea = 13; } catch (java.lang.RuntimeException t) { ea = 14; } catch (java.lang.Error t) { ea = 15; }
        long b = 0;
        int eb = 0;
        try { b = this_after.offsetToCommit(failedIndex); } catch (java.lang.NumberFormatException t) { eb = 1; } catch (java.lang.ArithmeticException t) { eb = 2; } catch (java.lang.NullPointerException t) { eb = 3; } catch (java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException t) { eb = 4; } catch (java.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException t) { eb = 5; } catch (java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException t) { eb = 6; } catch (java.lang.NegativeArraySizeException t) { eb = 7; } catch (java.lang.ClassCastException t) { eb = 8; } catch (java.lang.IllegalStateException t) { eb = 9; } catch (java.lang.IllegalArgumentException t) { eb = 10; } catch (java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException t) { eb = 11; } catch (java.util.NoSuchElementException t) { eb = 12; } catch (java.util.ConcurrentModificationException t) { eb = 13; } catch (java.lang.RuntimeException t) { eb = 14; } catch (java.lang.Error t) { eb = 15; }
        assert ea == eb && (ea != 0 || a == b);
    }
}
```
